text: Nine lessons ago, this whole project started with one sentence from the Merchandising Manager: can you show me how our product categories are doing this quarter, I want one dashboard I can pull up in the pricing review. Here's everything that sentence turned into.

Lesson one turned the vague ask into a specific, written requirement. Lessons two and three planned, then wrote, a real five-table T-SQL query across the category hierarchy. Lesson four connected that query to Power BI as a native query. Lessons five through seven sketched the layout, wrote three DAX measures, and added a slicer with formatting built for a non-technical reader. Lesson eight published it to the Power BI Service. And lesson nine practiced presenting it live, inside the actual pricing review.

None of those lessons were really about SQL or Power BI alone. Each one used those tools to practice something that transfers: requirements clarification, translating a question into correct data retrieval, validating data before trusting it, designing for a specific reader, delivering work in a usable form, and communicating results clearly. The tools were the vehicle -- these underlying skills are what actually made the project succeed.

This Beginner project deliberately left some things out: no subcategory-level drill-down, no multi-quarter trend, no pricing recommendations. That wasn't a limitation to apologize for -- it was the correct scope for what was actually asked, and knowing how to scope down is as real a skill as knowing how to scope up.

The Intermediate project in this capstone sequence picks up exactly where this one stopped on purpose: more stakeholders, and a comparison across time rather than a single quarter. The foundation doesn't change -- requirements clarification, correct T-SQL, and clear presentation -- but now it gets applied to a harder, more ambiguous ask.
That's the Beginner capstone, start to finish -- from one vague sentence to a published, presented dashboard, built on the same real AdventureWorks2012 data used throughout this course catalog.
